A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WSR research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained content, additions, and relocated limitations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality experiments, mobile runtime and memory measurements, and ablations across 13 real-world scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds camera-translation examples, a failure case, and a reported WebGL rendering-speed comparison.

M1.justification: The three WSR variants, view-dependent opacity, rendering equations, and training loss are retained. Appendix C newly describes densification, omitted opacity-threshold pruning, and culling; it does not establish that these procedures changed from v1.

E1.justification: The same 13 scenes from Mip-NeRF360, Tanks & Temples, and Deep Blending remain. Appendix C adds a targeted z-direction camera-translation scenario on Bicycle and Garden, extending the motion conditions examined beyond the existing rotational popping demonstration.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 6–8 add Compact 3DGS, Compressed 3DGS, and LightGaussian to the retained image-quality comparators. Appendix C adds a gsplat WebGL speed comparison. This substantially expands comparison with efficient Gaussian-splatting alternatives; their earlier citations alone were not evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a camera-translation test comparing EXP-WSR and LC-WSR and a separate WebGL FPS comparison. Existing benchmark metrics, mobile hardware, and 1920 × 1080 timing settings remain unchanged. The WebGL protocol is unclear because its paragraph mentions both equal and lower rendering resolutions.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds a qualitative check for color shifts during z-direction camera motion; Figure 8 adds a transparency failure case. The WSR-variant, learnable-parameter, and view-dependent-opacity ablations and the original popping analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new FPS range is not identified as statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands aggregate and per-scene baseline results and reports 30 FPS versus 19–25 FPS for gsplat WebGL, plus new qualitative findings. All retained result values are unchanged. The additions contain reporting errors: Table 7 repeats the new baselines' PSNR values as SSIM, and Compact 3DGS Deep Blending PSNR differs between Table 1 (29.79) and Table 6 (29.46).

T1.justification: Section 3 removes v1's explicit sorting-index definition and depth-order inequality, Eq. 6, while retaining the sorting requirement in prose. The rendering, weighting, and opacity equations otherwise remain unchanged apart from renumbering; no proofs or theorems are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: sort-free rendering compatible with graphics hardware, learned WSR and view-dependent opacity, competitive image quality, elimination of sorting-induced popping, and average 1.23× mobile acceleration.

C2.justification: v2 discusses z-motion behavior and apparent transparency of dark foreground objects, attributing the failure to suboptimal training. Section 5.2 adds a tentative cache-miss explanation for GPU slowdowns and distinguishes runtime memory from storage footprint. The existing early-termination limitation is relocated, not newly introduced.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents retained 3DGS densification, omitted opacity-threshold pruning, frustum culling, and hardware accumulation. Section 5.2 explains using RGBA alpha slots for opacity coefficients and the increased storage footprint. These are additional implementation disclosures, without demonstrated changes to existing settings.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but v2 integrates previously cited compact-Gaussian methods into its related-work discussion and comparisons, makes its relationship to OIT more explicit, and introduces gsplat WebGL as a practical comparison point.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain intact. v2 adds Appendix C, moves the existing limitations and future-work discussion to Appendix D, makes localized explanatory edits, and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR 2025 publication header.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 7–8 and expands Tables 1 and 6–8 with comparator rows. Existing figures retain their visual content, while some displays are resized or relocated, including Figure 5 and Table 5. Captions and spacing receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves implementation disclosure and adds useful motion diagnostics and an explicit failure case. However, its expanded comparison evidence introduces clear reliability problems: Table 7 duplicates PSNR values as SSIM, and several baseline summaries disagree with appendix values. The WebGL timing conditions are also unclear. With the original central results unchanged, these benefits and reporting harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
